title: Secondary education project plan swaps library money for laptops
excerpt: A revised World Bank-funded project would give laptops to 30,000 top SSC students and cut library grants by about half. The bank must agree.
content:
A revised plan for a World Bank-funded secondary education project would spend Tk 900 crore on laptops for top SSC students, 100 pilot electric buses and solar panels at 2,000 schools and madrasahs, The Business Standard reported on 18 November. To save money, the plan cuts library grants and recommends scrapping central book buying.

Key figures

  • Project cost would rise from Tk 3,304.08 crore to Tk 3,659.75 crore
  • Laptops for 30,000 students who got GPA-5, at Tk 1 lakh each
  • Library grants would fall from Tk 118.48 crore to Tk 60 crore
  • The project covers 29,621 institutions and is backed by $300 million from the World Bank's International Development Association (IDA)

The project's targets for 2028 include 65% of Grade 8 students reaching minimum proficiency in Bangla and 90% in maths, and 74% of students staying in school through Grade 10. The Economic Relations Division is reviewing the proposal, and it needs the World Bank's consent.

Why it matters

The change moves donor money for secondary schools away from libraries, which every pupil can use, towards devices for the highest scorers. Education NGOs that work on learning poverty, girls' retention and rural schools may want to ask how the new items will help the project meet its own learning and retention targets.

What to watch

Whether the World Bank agrees to the revision, and whether the government sets out how the laptops and e-buses link to the project's results.

Sources
